issues.legal_issue: A revenue mutation entry does not create or extinguish title to property and has no presumptive value as proof of title.
material_facts: The disputed land had been mutated in the revenue records in the name of a person who claimed to be an heir and later sold the land.
The lower appellate court treated the mutation as establishing the seller’s title.
issues.conclusion: The mutation did not confer title on the person recorded or enable her to pass title to the purchasers.
issues.legal_principle: Mutation in revenue records serves to enable collection of land revenue from the person recorded; it neither creates nor extinguishes title and has no presumptive value on title. No earlier case or specific statutory provision was cited for this principle.

predicates.land_title_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a claim to title in land.
predicates.revenue_mutation_recorded: A person’s name was entered in revenue records by mutation.
predicates.title_inferred_from_mutation: A decision-maker treated the mutation entry as establishing that person’s title.

issues.definition: When a land-title proceeding relies on a revenue mutation as proof of title, the mutation does not establish title.

issues.legal_issue: A lower appellate court cannot properly reverse a trial court’s reasoned finding on a material factual issue without considering the supporting evidence and reasons.
material_facts: The trial court considered oral and documentary evidence and gave reasons for finding which person was the deceased landowner’s daughter.

The lower appellate court did not discuss the oral evidence or the trial court’s reasons, did not set aside the trial court’s finding on that issue, and made no positive finding supporting the competing claim.
The lower appellate court nevertheless reversed the trial court’s decree.
issues.conclusion: The lower appellate court’s failure to consider the material evidence and the trial court’s reasons vitiated its conclusion, and its judgment was unsustainable.
issues.legal_principle: A lower appellate court’s conclusion is vitiated when it reverses a trial court’s finding without considering the material evidence and reasons supporting that finding. No specific statutory provision or earlier case was cited for this principle.

rule.if: civil_appeal_from_trial_decree and trial_court_made_reasoned_factual_finding and lower_appellate_court_reversed_finding and material_evidence_not_considered

predicates.civil_appeal_from_trial_decree: The proceeding is an appeal from a trial court’s decree in a civil case.
predicates.trial_court_made_reasoned_factual_findin: The trial court made a factual finding after considering evidence and giving reasons.
predicates.lower_appellate_court_reversed_finding: The lower appellate court reversed the trial court’s decree or factual finding.
predicates.material_evidence_not_considered: The lower appellate court did not consider material evidence or the trial court’s reasons supporting the finding.

issues.definition: In a civil appeal from a trial decree, reversing a reasoned factual finding without considering its supporting evidence vitiates the appellate reversal.

issues.legal_issue: A plaintiff claiming an interest for herself and an interest for the heirs of a co-heir may bring a suit asserting those claimed interests.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought to recover the share claimed for herself and a share claimed for the husband and sons of another alleged daughter of the deceased landowner.
The lower appellate court held that the plaintiff could not sue in respect of that other share.
issues.conclusion: The lower appellate court was wrong to hold that the plaintiff could not file the suit on the stated claims.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the plaintiff could file the suit where she claimed an interest for herself and an interest in favour of the other alleged daughter’s husband and sons. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited for this holding.

predicates.civil_property_suit: The proceeding is a civil suit concerning rights in property.
predicates.plaintiff_claims_own_interest: The plaintiff asserts an interest in the disputed property for herself.
predicates.plaintiff_claims_interest_for_coheirs: The plaintiff also asserts an interest in the disputed property for the heirs of another person said to share in the property.

issues.definition: In a civil property suit, a plaintiff who claims an interest for herself and for the heirs of another alleged co-heir may sue on those claimed interests.

issues.legal_issue: A court deciding a property dispute cannot ignore a relevant will and an unannulled succession certificate and the rights flowing from them.
material_facts: The widow of the original owner had executed a will concerning the estate in favour of two alleged daughters.
A civil court had issued a succession certificate in favour of those two claimants.
The opposing defendants had not sought to annul the succession certificate on grounds available under the Indian Succession Act.
The lower appellate court did not consider the will and succession certificate.
issues.conclusion: The will, the succession certificate, and the rights flowing from the certificate could not be ignored; the lower appellate court erred by failing to consider them.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the will and the rights flowing from the succession certificate issued under the Indian Succession Act were relevant and could not be ignored, particularly where no attempt had been made to annul the certificate on grounds available under that Act. No earlier case was cited.

rule.if: property_inheritance_proceeding and relevant_will_exists and succession_certificate_issued and certificate_not_challenged_for_annulment and instruments_not_considered

predicates.property_inheritance_proceeding: The proceeding concerns property claimed through inheritance or succession.
predicates.relevant_will_exists: The deceased person executed a will concerning the estate in favour of persons claiming an interest.
predicates.succession_certificate_issued: A court issued a succession certificate in favour of persons claiming an interest in the estate.
predicates.certificate_not_challenged_for_annulment: No party sought annulment of the succession certificate on available grounds.
predicates.instruments_not_considered: The decision-maker failed to consider the relevant will or succession certificate and the rights flowing from them.

issues.definition: In a property inheritance proceeding, when a relevant will and an unannulled succession certificate exist, failing to consider them and the rights flowing from the certificate is improper.
